# Function

The function algebra — Field's first-class, evolvable, graph-rewritable notion of a function. Build them, compose them, fit them, mutate them, and rewrite their graphs with user-authored patterns.

## FnMetric.kt { #fnmetric-kt }

The objective shared by both halves of the function-search family: [`FnMetric`](function.md#fnmetric-kt-fnmetric), a `fun interface`
scoring a candidate signal against a target on one even sample grid (lower is better), plus a
companion of ready-made metrics — `rmse`, `mae`, `lp`, `maxError`, `huber`, `logCosh`,
`correlation` — and the `fromResidual` / `window` builders behind them.

`FnMetric.lossAgainst` turns a metric into the `(Fn) -> Double` closure the gradient fitters in
FunctionFit.kt descend, sampling the target once and reusing it across the finite-difference
inner loop; the same metrics are what `matchFitness` in FunctionEvolve.kt negates, so structural
search and numeric fitting can run under one notion of "close". Any metric — including a
hand-written lambda — must ignore indices where either side is non-finite and return
`Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` when no index is jointly finite, which callers read as maximally bad.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FnMetric.kt`

### FnMetric { #fnmetric-kt-fnmetric }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">FnMetric</span></code>

A pluggable distance metric between a target signal and a candidate, evaluated on a shared even sample grid. **Lower is better**; `0.0` means the candidate matches the target at every sampled point. This is the objective the differentiable fitters (`fitGradient`, `fitBest`, `fitHybrid`) descend, and it generalises the RMSE they used to hard-code.

Lower is better; returns `Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` when the two share no jointly-finite sample. |

## FunctionEvolve.kt { #functionevolve-kt }

Search over the *structure* of `Fn` graphs — the genetic counterpart to the gradient fitting of
a fixed structure's numbers in FunctionFit.kt.

[`FnMutations`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnmutations) holds the seeded mutation operators (jitter and nudge numeric leaves, transmute an
op within its `OpRegistry` family, prune, duplicate or graft a subtree), each expressed over the
graph copy and query primitives rather than a private traversal. `evolve` runs them as a bounded
(µ+λ) hill-climb and returns an [`FnEvolveRun`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnevolverun) listing every accepted improvement. Fitness is the
caller's: `matchFitness` scores closeness to a target under any `FnMetric`, less an optional
complexity penalty from `graphMetrics`; `noveltyFitness` instead scores distance from an archive
of [`FnBehaviour`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnbehaviour) descriptors — what a graph *does* when sampled, not how it is built — and
`evolveVariety` chains slots of novelty search into a behaviourally spread set of results rather
than one best match.

Both runners are bounded by an iteration count so a search cannot disappear into an animation
loop, and both are deterministic: traversal is stable and every draw comes from one seeded
`Random`, with each `evolveVariety` slot deriving `rngSeed * 31 + slot`. Set `normalize` on
`Functions.Fn.behaviour` (and hence on novelty search) to compare shape rather than amplitude.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionEvolve.kt`

## FunctionFit.kt { #functionfit-kt }

Gradient-based fitting of `Fn` graphs — the differentiable counterpart to the genetic
`evolve` in FunctionEvolve.kt.

Where `evolve` searches over *structure* (seeded mutation of the graph), this file tunes
the *numbers*: the numeric leaves of a fixed-structure graph are the θ-vector, and Adam
descends the RMSE loss against a target `Fn`. The two are complementary — `fitHybrid`
runs `evolve` to discover a shape, then polishes its constants here.

A lone `fitGradient` is *local* and will stall in a frequency local-minimum when the seed's
oscillator frequencies are far from the target's (RMSE-vs-frequency is periodic, not convex);
`fitBest` wraps it in deterministic jittered restarts and is the recommended entry when the
starting numbers may be wrong. See `fitBest`'s KDoc for the why.

The θ extract/apply primitives ride on `Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers`, whose post-order
DFS is stable and deterministic with `preserveSharing = false`: the *i*-th numeric leaf
seen while reading is the *i*-th leaf written while applying, so a plain index counter is
a sound θ↔graph bijection. Everything is deterministic given a seed (Adam itself has no
randomness; only an optional [`FnFitConfig`](function.md#functionfit-kt-fnfitconfig) init-jitter draws from a single `Random`),
which is what makes a fitted gesture reproducible in live art — the same discipline as
[`FnEvolveRun`](function.md#functionevolve-kt-fnevolverun).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionFit.kt`

**Used in:** [Differentiating Functions](../autodiff_examples.md), [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md), [Patterns: writing rhythm as a function of time](../pattern_language.md)

## FunctionGraph.kt { #functiongraph-kt }

The data model and the copy engine underneath Field's graph-rewritable notion of a function:
[`FnGraphNode`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphnode) / [`FnGraphEdge`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphedge) (an op name, role-tagged children, scalar metadata and an
optional rebuild recipe) plus `Functions.Fn.deepCopy` and `Functions.Fn.rewriteGraph`, a
bottom-up copy that offers every occurrence to an [`FnGraphEdit`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphedit). Every other file in this
family runs on that single traversal, as do the edit primitives declared here —
`Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers`, `Functions.Fn.replaceOps`, `Functions.Fn.pruneWhere`,
`Functions.Fn.graftWhere`, `Functions.Fn.duplicateWhere`, `Functions.Fn.slideCopy`. The
read-only renderings live here too: `Functions.Fn.graphSnapshot`, `Functions.Fn.graphText`,
`Functions.Fn.graphSvg` and `Functions.Fn.graphFLineMap`.

Two constraints show up everywhere downstream. A node whose `rebuild` is null cannot be
reconstructed, so a copy keeps the original evaluator and drops the recipe. And
`preserveSharing` decides whether a shared subgraph stays shared (memoized by identity) or is
expanded into a tree — `Functions.Fn.deepCopy` defaults it to true, while the rewriting entry
points default it to false so each occurrence can be edited independently.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraph.kt`

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md), [Patterns: writing rhythm as a function of time](../pattern_language.md)

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">graphNode</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnGraphNode</span></code> | This function's graph node — or a synthetic `"opaque"` node, tagged `opaque`, when it has no graph at all. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">deepCopy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">preserveSharing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">edit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnGraphEdit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">FnGraphEdit</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="n">&#95;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">copy</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="n">copy</span> <span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span></code> | Rebuilds this function from its graph, bottom-up, offering every node to `edit` on the way — the single traversal every other rewrite in this family is written in terms of. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">rewriteGraph</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">preserveSharing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">edit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnGraphEdit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span></code> | `deepCopy` under the name that says what you are doing, and with sharing **off** by default so each occurrence of a repeated subgraph is offered to `edit` separately and can be changed independently. |

Same quiet no-op if the transmutation is not viable. |

## FunctionGraphBrowser.kt { #functiongraphbrowser-kt }

The looking-at-it layer for the `Fn` graph family: sample a graph on one shared time-base, then
render it as a self-contained interactive HTML browser.

`Functions.Fn.graphTrace` samples every visible occurrence three ways — `local` (that subgraph
alone), `muted` (the whole root with the occurrence replaced by a neutral constant: `0.0`, or
`1.0` for a divisor) and `effect` (`final - muted`) — plus optional value sweeps for numeric
nodes, and `Functions.Fn.graphBrowseHtml` / `Functions.Fn.browseGraph` wrap that in a canvas UI.
`Functions.Fn.graphRewriteTrace` is the same idea for rewriting: it applies rules cumulatively
— either `FnGraphRule`s or the meaningful lines of a string-DSL spec — recording before, after
and delta per stage for `FnRewriteTrace.rewriteBrowseHtml` and `Functions.Fn.browseRewrite`.

`effect` is a counterfactual, not an additive decomposition: it includes every transformation
between the occurrence and the root. Tracing is bounded by `maxDepth`/`maxNodes` and sampling is
NaN-safe (out-of-domain and throwing evaluations become `NaN` and are simply left undrawn). The
`browse*` functions display into the current box and throw without an active `Box.context`; the
`*Html` functions are pure strings and work anywhere.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphBrowser.kt`

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

## FunctionGraphRules.kt { #functiongraphrules-kt }

The query and rule-runner layer over the graph copier in FunctionGraph.kt.

Queries come first, and none of them copy or evaluate the function:
`Functions.Fn.graphMatches` and `Functions.Fn.firstGraphMatch` visit a shared node once per
incoming path, so role, ancestry, depth and path stay meaningful for editing;
`Functions.Fn.graphMetrics` separates unique DAG nodes from occurrences and charges a
caller-supplied cost; `Functions.Fn.graphSignature` reduces structure to a deterministic string
with evaluator closures and rebuild lambdas deliberately excluded. On top of those, [`FnGraphRule`](function.md#functiongraphrules-kt-fngraphrule)
pairs a named predicate with a replacement, and `Functions.Fn.rewriteWithRules` (one bottom-up
pass) and `Functions.Fn.rewriteUntilStable` (repeated passes) apply them, returning an
[`FnGraphRewriteRun`](function.md#functiongraphrules-kt-fngraphrewriterun) that records every edit that actually changed a node's signature.

Fixed-point rewriting is bounded on purpose: `Functions.Fn.rewriteUntilStable` compares
signatures each pass and reports `FnGraphRewriteStop.STABLE`, `FnGraphRewriteStop.CYCLE` or
`FnGraphRewriteStop.MAX_PASSES` rather than letting a non-terminating rule set hide inside an
animation loop. Rules default to `FnGraphRuleMode.FIRST_MATCH` at each node, so ordering is
explicit; `FnGraphRuleMode.ALL_MATCHES` chains every matching rule on the same copy.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionGraphRules.kt`

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

## FunctionOps.kt { #functionops-kt }

The op vocabulary for the whole `Fn` graph family, held in one object, [`OpRegistry`](function.md#functionops-kt-opregistry): which op
names the stdlib actually emits into a graph node, which of them are aliases of each other, and
which can be rebuilt from an arbitrary node's role-addressed children — those rebuildable ones
each carrying a family label (oscillator, noise, transform, …).

Everything that has to reason about ops consults it instead of keeping a private list — the
rewrite DSL's `op=` validator and its hint text, the pattern matcher's alias-aware op
comparison, `rebuildAsOp`, and the "another op in the same family" draw behind the
`substituteOp` mutation. The Monaco `fnrewrite.js` extension mirrors it, and a JVM test asserts
that mirror never drifts.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionOps.kt`

## FunctionRewriteDsl.kt { #functionrewritedsl-kt }

The `selector => action` string rewrite DSL, compiled and applied end to end.
`compileFnRewrite` parses a spec into an [`FnRewriteProgram`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewriteprogram) carrying line/column
[`FnRewriteDiagnostic`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewritediagnostic)s; `Functions.Fn.rewrite`, `Functions.Fn.previewRewrite` (which also
reports match paths and which rules did nothing) and `Functions.Fn.rewriteChecked` (which
refuses an invalid program) run it over the graph copier. Selector matching lives here — op,
role, name, tag and depth tokens, `parent=`, `[key>=n]` predicates and slash-separated path
selectors with `*` and `**` wildcards — and so does action application: `op=`, `name=`,
`domain=`, `drop`, and the numeric `=`, `*=`, `/=`, `+=`, `-=` forms. `op=` targets are checked
against `OpRegistry`; an unknown op is reported as a warning, not an error.

The file deliberately does not depend on the live-code compiler. A Kotlin right-hand side is
parsed out of its `@{...}` (or dollar-brace) wrapper and then handed to
`FnRewriteOptions.kotlinNumberContext`; when no caller supplied one, the action is simply not
applied. FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt is what plugs a box's Kotlin engine into that hook, and
FunctionRewritePattern.kt is the separate structural pattern-to-template surface.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteDsl.kt`

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">rewrite</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">spec</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">options</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnRewriteOptions</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">FnRewriteOptions</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Functions</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Fn</span></code> | Compiles `spec` and applies it, returning a new function and discarding everything the attempt learned — the forgiving one-liner for sketching and performance. |

Consulted only when `kotlinNumberContext` is absent *or* returns null, so it also works as a fallback under it. |

False — expand — because that is what makes path-sensitive selectors behave the way you would guess; see `Functions.Fn.deepCopy`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kotlinNumberContext</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">FnRewriteNumberContext</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The preferred hook: given the matched node wrapped as an [`FnRewriteNumberContext`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewritenumbercontext), return the new number, or null to leave the value alone. Returning null falls through to `kotlinNumber`. |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">program</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnRewriteProgram</span></code> | The compiled spec, including the diagnostics that did not stop it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">applications</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FnRewriteApplication</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every rule/occurrence pair that fired, in traversal order (bottom-up, so children first). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">matchedRules</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many distinct rules found at least one node. Compare with `program.rules.size`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">matchCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Total matches across all rules — one per rule per occurrence, so easily larger than the rule count. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">changeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many of those matches changed the graph. The gap between this and `matchCount` is the no-ops. |

Treat these as hypotheses to reconsider, not as success. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">summary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Compact deterministic report suitable for logs, chat, and agent transcripts. |

## FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt { #functionrewritekotlin-kt }

The bridge that gives the string rewrite DSL a real Kotlin right-hand side.

FunctionRewriteDsl.kt parses `@{...}` expressions but never compiles them; this file supplies
the `FnRewriteOptions.kotlinNumberContext` hook it leaves open, compiling each expression as a
`FnRewriteNumberContext -> Any?` lambda inside a live box's coding context so a snippet can read
`value`, `op`, `parentOp`, `depth` and the rest as plain properties.
[`SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberExpression`](function.md#functionrewritekotlin-kt-sourcebackedfnrewritenumberexpression) stores only source plus a box id and hydrates on first
use; [`SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberEvaluator`](function.md#functionrewritekotlin-kt-sourcebackedfnrewritenumberevaluator) caches one per distinct expression string. The entry
points are `Functions.Fn.rewriteKotlin`, `Functions.Fn.previewRewriteKotlin`,
`Functions.Fn.rewriteKotlinChecked` and the `Box.rewriteFn` / `Box.previewRewriteFn` receiver
forms — each is the corresponding plain-DSL call with that evaluator wired in.

Hydration requires the originating box to still be loaded and the compiled lambda to return a
`Number?`; anything else throws, naming the box or the offending source. When
there is no box in scope no evaluator is installed at all, so Kotlin right-hand sides are left
unapplied and the compiler-free `rewrite(...)` path is unaffected.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/FunctionRewriteKotlin.kt`

**Used in:** [Functions to FLine examples (Field graphics)](../functions_examples.md)

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">fnRewriteNumberExpression</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">context</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberExpression</span></code> | Wraps a snippet of Kotlin source as a rewrite-number evaluator bound to `box`, compiled lazily on first use. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">fnRewriteNumber</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">block</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnRewriteNumberContext</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SourceBackedFnRewriteNumberExpression</span></code> | A rewrite-number evaluator written as an ordinary Kotlin lambda over [`FnRewriteNumberContext`](function.md#functionrewritedsl-kt-fnrewritenumbercontext), with no compilation involved — the typed alternative to a string of source. |

## FunctionRewritePattern.kt { #functionrewritepattern-kt }

The third rewriting surface in the family, and the algebraic one. FunctionRewriteDsl.kt is
`selector => action` and edits one matched node in place; `FnGraphRule` in FunctionGraphRules.kt
is a hand-written predicate plus a hand-written replacement; here both sides of a rule are graph
shapes with metavariables ([`FnPattern`](function.md#functionrewritepattern-kt-fnpattern)), so `add(?x, 0) => ?x` reads as an identity rather than
an instruction. `fnRule` compiles a spec into an ordinary `FnGraphRule`, which is what lets
pattern rules reuse the existing traced, bounded, cycle-detecting runners;
`Functions.Fn.rewritePatterns` is the fixed-point convenience over a set of specs.

Matching and the parser are both here. A `?name` binds a subtree and, if repeated, must bind a
structurally equal one (compared by `graphSignature()`); a bare number matches a numeric node's
`value` to within 1e-12; op names are compared through `OpRegistry`'s alias table; `op(a, b, …)`
constrains only the leading children. The string template side is narrower than the pattern
side: a bare op transmutes the matched node, only add/subtract/multiply/divide accept an
explicit child list, and any other `op(...)` template throws — the `fnRule` overload taking a
Kotlin builder over [`FnPatternMatch`](function.md#functionrewritepattern-kt-fnpatternmatch) is the general escape.

## autodiff_fn.kt { #autodiff-fn-kt }

Differentiating the `Fn` graph itself — the bridge that makes `autodiff.kt` a *Field* capability
rather than a generic AD library.

`Functions.Fn` is a closure over `Double`, so it cannot be differentiated by overloading its
arithmetic. But every `Fn` the stdlib builds also carries an inspectable [`FnGraphNode`](function.md#functiongraph-kt-fngraphnode): the op
name, the role-tagged children, the scalar metadata. This file **re-interprets that structure in
[`AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) arithmetic**, so the exact derivative of a graph's output with respect to its numeric leaves
— the same θ-vector `extractParameters` reads and `applyParameters` writes — falls out of one
backward sweep instead of `2n` extra evaluations.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
with(Functions) {
    val f = sin(1.5, amplitude = 0.8, offset = 0.2)
    f.gradientAt(0.3)          // d f(0.3) / d theta, exact, in leaf order
}
```

### Which ops, and how the honesty is enforced

The interpreter covers the smooth algebraic core — see `FnAutoDiff.differentiableOps`. That is
deliberately a *subset*: the piecewise oscillators (`saw`, `square`), the table-backed
interpolants, the noise generators and everything with baked point data are not here, and
`FnAutoDiff.supports` answers honestly for any graph.

The danger with a second interpreter is that it silently computes the derivative of a *different
function* from the one `eval` computes. So the exact path never trusts itself: `FnAutoDiff.agrees`
re-evaluates the interpreter against `Functions.Fn.eval` on the caller's own sample grid and
reports the worst disagreement, and the fitters run that check before switching over. A mismatch
demotes the run to finite differences rather than returning a confident wrong gradient.

### Ops indexed by leaf, not by node

θ-indices are assigned by exactly the traversal `Functions.Fn.mapGraphNumbers` uses — post-order
DFS over `node.children` in order, one index per node carrying `numbers["value"]` — so index *i*
here is the same leaf as index *i* in `extractParameters`. `FnAutoDiff.leafIndices` is that map,
keyed by the child-index path, and a test asserts the two agree leaf for leaf.

## autodiff_formula.kt { #autodiff-formula-kt }

One declaration of each `Fn` op's pointwise semantics, walked by two evaluators — so `Fn.eval` and
the reverse-mode gradient cannot compute different functions.

### The problem this solves

`autodiff_fn.kt`'s first draft re-implemented each op's formula in [`AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) arithmetic beside the
hand-written `Double` closure in `Functions.kt`. That is two transcriptions of one truth, and the
only thing holding them together was a runtime value-agreement check that *fell back* on
disagreement. A guard is a safety net, not a structure: the two would drift the first time an op's
formula changed, and the fallback would hide it.

So the per-op formula now lives in exactly one place — [`FnFormulas`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnformulas) — as a tiny expression tree
([`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr)) over the op's role-addressed children and the sample position `x`. Two walkers consume
it:

- `evalFormula` in `Double`, transcribed to be **bit-identical** to the hand-written closure
  (same operations, same order, same `Math.pow` / `coerceIn` calls);
- `evalFormulaAD` in tracked [`AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) arithmetic.

The AD side therefore has **no per-op code at all**. Adding an op means adding one [`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr); the
gradient follows for free, and the number of places a transcription error can hide drops from
"once per op" to "once per [`FnExpr`](function.md#autodiff-formula-kt-fnexpr) kind" — and each kind is oracle-checked once.

`AutoDiffFnBridgeTest.theFormulaTableIsABitIdenticalTranscriptionOfFnEval` closes the loop: for
every op with a formula it asserts the `Double` walker's output is bit-identical (`toRawBits`) to
`Functions`' own `eval` across a grid **and** at perturbed parameters. A formula that is not a
faithful transcription cannot reach `main`.

### Why `Fn.eval` is not simply replaced by the walker

It could be, and the seam is a single one: every op in `Functions` builds its `Fn` through one
private factory, `graphFn(domain, name, op, …, eval: (Double) -> Double)` at `Functions.kt:886`, so
a formula-derived evaluator could be substituted there without touching the individual factories.

It is not, and the reason is measured rather than assumed. `FnFormulaBenchmarkTest` times the walk
against the closure on the same graphs, warmed, best of five rounds of 400k evaluations:

| graph | hand-written closure | formula walk | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sin(1.5, …)` | 14.4 ns | 67.5 ns | **4.67×** |
| `cos(2) * sin(1.5, …)` | 47.3 ns | 161.9 ns | **3.42×** |
| `gaussian(…) * sin(…)` | 56.8 ns | 193.3 ns | **3.40×** |

A 3.4–4.7× tax on `Fn.eval` is not payable: it is the hottest call in the library, and one
`fitGradient` at the defaults is ~8.7·10⁵ whole-graph evaluations, with plotting, `FnMetric`,
`evolve` and every sampler on the same path. The cost is the per-node `when` dispatch and the
`Child` role lookup (a linear scan of `node.children`) against a closure the JIT inlines wholesale.

So the shape landed on is: **one declaration, two walkers, and a test-time proof they agree.** The
formula table is the only place an op's semantics are written for differentiation purposes, the AD
side has no per-op code, and `theFormulaTableIsABitIdenticalTranscriptionOfFnEval` compares the
`Double` walk against `Fn.eval` as **raw bits** across a 129-point grid at three parameter vectors
for every op. That is strictly stronger than the runtime value-agreement guard for preventing
*drift* — it fails in CI rather than silently demoting a run — and it costs nothing at sample time.
The runtime guard stays, because it also catches the cases the table cannot express at all (an
unbounded shape domain, an inverted `clamp` range).

If the walk ever needs to be the only traversal, the two costs to attack first are the role lookup
(pre-resolve `Child(role)` to a child index when the formula is built) and the recursive `when`
(flatten to a post-order array of opcodes with a value stack). Neither is done here.

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ops</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Set</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every op with a declared formula, lower-cased. |

### FnOpStatus { #autodiff-formula-kt-fnopstatus }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FnOpStatus</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">reason</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closable</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">missing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Why an `Fn` op has no derivative, and whether that is permanent.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">reason</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | One line, in prose, for a diagnostic or a docs table. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closable</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True when a derivative could be written; false when there genuinely is not one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">missing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What is missing, when `closable`. Empty otherwise. |

### FnNonDifferentiable { #autodiff-formula-kt-fnnondifferentiable }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">FnNonDifferentiable</span></code>

Every op in [`OpRegistry`](function.md#functionops-kt-opregistry) that [`FnAutoDiff`](function.md#autodiff-fn-kt-fnautodiff) cannot differentiate, with a declared reason.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">statusOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">op</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FnOpStatus</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The declared status of `op`, or null when this op has a formula (or is unknown to the registry). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ops</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Set</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every op declared non-differentiable, lower-cased. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closable</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Ops whose derivative could be written but has not been — the honest backlog. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">explain</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">op</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A one-line explanation for a diagnostic: either the declared reason, or a note that the op is differentiable, or that nothing is known about it. |

</div>
